chief_complaint: Extensive, painful verrucous skin lesions on his left foot and lower leg.
history_of_present_illness: Ten years prior, he had a leech bite on the dorsum of his left foot, followed a week later by a small painless red nodule that slowly increased in size and spread up to his knee over years, with the ankle becoming painful and swollen three days before admission.
exposure_and_epidemiology: A 72-year-old male farmer from a provincial hospital in northern Laos with a history of a leech bite on his left foot 10 years prior.
vitals: Vital signs are normal and the patient is afebrile.
physical_exam: The left lower leg and foot were grossly swollen, hyperaemic, and hot, with several cauliflower-like masses and oval plaque-like lesions that were partly erythematous, partly fungating, purulent, and oozing a bad odour.
labs_and_diagnostics: Radiography of the left leg and foot showed no bone involvement. Direct microscopy of skin scrapings revealed characteristic brownish, round, thick-walled, multiseptate sclerotic cells typical of chromoblastomycosis, with fungal cells more readily visible using 10% potassium hydroxide solution. PCR from skin tissue was positive and sequencing revealed 100% similarity with Fonsecaea pedrosoi, F. monophora and F. nubica. Liver function tests and serum glucose were monitored during treatment and remained normal.
differential_diagnosis: Sporotrichosis, chromoblastomycosis, mycetoma (Madura Foot), mycobacterial infections (cutaneous tuberculosis, lepromatous leprosy, atypical mycobacteria), cutaneous leishmaniasis, Kaposi's Sarcoma (in HIV-positive patients), squamous cell carcinoma, sarcoidosis, chronic eczema, psoriasis, bacterial superinfection, and deep vein thrombosis.
management_and_clinical_course: Secondary bacterial superinfection was suspected, leading to local iodine-based antiseptics and oral antibiotics (initially cloxacillin and metronidazole, later co-trimoxazole after Escherichia coli was cultured from pus). Antifungal treatment was initiated with itraconazole (400 mg/d for 7 days monthly pulse therapy) and surgical debridement of all lesions. Oral terbinafine (initially 500 mg/d, later 750 mg/d) was added for 9 months along with local terbinafine ointment for 6 months. The lesions healed uneventfully with some residual swelling and hypopigmentation.
